regime_context: The detector is in a narrow-rotation state: only Banks (rank 2, score 0.708) passes the absolute-trend eligibility gate, while the nominal leader Coal (rank 1, score 0.735) is not eligible, leaving breadth of eligible themes at just 1 of 22. Critically, the gate_helps flag is false for this market — the trend discipline did not reduce drawdown on China A-shares history and the tape mean-reverts — so even the one eligible theme should be treated as experimental/display, not an edge. Given the weak track record (dir_accuracy 0.366) and no validated forward edge in rotation timing, I am issuing only two low-conviction, falsifiable leans rather than padding this note.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Banks' eligibility (the only eligible theme) persists and whether the near-tie between Coal and Banks (margin 0.027) resolves into a confirmed handoff where Banks overtakes Coal on score AND Coal loses its rank-1 spot with Banks' durability_bar holding above 0.7 — either resolution would retire this watch.

theses.subject: Banks
theses.thesis: Banks is the ONLY theme passing the absolute-trend eligibility gate, with the strongest durability bar (0.8), high breadth (0.833), and a trend hurst tag — the detector's trend-health leg is genuinely supportive. However, the same state shows crowding_z of 1.77 and crowded=true, and the guardrails explicitly forbid treating the leader as a buy because it leads, and forbid fading it on a crowding flag. Since gate_helps is false (the trend gate did not cut drawdown on this market's mean-reverting history), there is no validated discipline edge to lean on. The honest read is: trend-health says 'staying power,' but no alpha edge and heavy crowding cap the case. I lean avoid, not overweight, because the one leg that works elsewhere (absolute-trend gate) is known to fail here, so a directional overweight would be overconfidence.
evidence: eligible=true, only theme passing the absolute-trend gate
gate_helps=false — trend discipline did not reduce drawdown on China A-shares history
theses.dissent: Banks may be the only place where trend-following capital can hide in a mean-reverting tape; high durability and breadth suggest the move is not exhausted, and avoiding the sole eligible theme leaves no alternative within the detector's own discipline. The crowding flag is explicitly a size-down caution, not an exit signal.

theses.subject: Coal
theses.thesis: Coal is the nominal momentum leader (rank 1, score 0.735) but fails the absolute-trend eligibility gate (eligible=false, durability_bar only 0.25, hurst_tag=mixed) and shows weak breadth (0.3). Per the detector's own validated discipline, only eligible themes qualify for trend-following allocation, and the guardrails explicitly prohibit treating the momentum rank as a return forecast or buy list. The rotation radar shows Coal as 'leader' with a razor-thin margin (0.027) over Banks and directional=false — no confirmed handoff, just noise-level separation. I lean avoid because the theme carries leadership optics without the trend-health gate's blessing, and the only validated use of the gate is to avoid exactly this kind of whipsaw-prone exposure.
evidence: rank=1, score=0.735 (momentum leader — an attention lens, not alpha)
eligible=false, durability_bar=0.25, hurst_tag=mixed (does not pass trend-health gate)
rotation.margin=0.027, directional=false (no confirmed handoff, near-tie with Banks)
theses.dissent: The market is mean-reverting (gate_helps=false), so ignoring the trend gate and leaning INTO the momentum leader could actually be the right reflexive trade here — Coal may continue to front-run precisely because the discipline that would exclude it is known to be broken on this tape.
